name: skill-eval
title: Answering questions about past work
command: eval/skill_eval.py run --set all --cond C,H && eval/skill_eval.py grade RUN

conditions.questions: 90, written from real sessions in 10 projects and reviewed against the code so that only session history answers them
conditions.source: the author's own session archive; only counts leave it
conditions.answering model: Claude Sonnet, a fresh process per question
conditions.grading model: Claude Opus, blind, both conditions in one shuffled pass

summary: Agents answer questions whose answers exist only in past sessions. Both conditions have ctx and its skill; one also gets the one-line note that the session-start hook adds.

metrics.label: Questions where the note did better

bar: score no lower, no more wrong answers, tokens up at most 15%
baseline: the same agent with ctx and its skill but without the session-start note
meaning: Telling the agent at session start that an archive exists is worth about 7 questions in 90 and costs no extra tokens. The difference is borderline by a sign test (p = 0.052), so it is kept as likely but not proven.
